title: Needs vs wants
card1: Needs keep you housed, fed, working and safe.
card2: Wants are everything else. That's okay. Wants aren't bad.
card3: You pick a fun-money limit for wants. Everything above it gets a new job.

title: Why $1,000 comes first
card1: A flat tire. A vet bill. A surprise copay. Life happens to everyone.
card2: Without a cushion, a surprise lands on a credit card and the debt grows. $1,000 set aside breaks that cycle.
card3: It's a starter amount, not the finish line. A bigger safety net comes later, once the debt is gone.

title: Where to keep it
card1: Keep your cushion in its own savings account, apart from the money you spend.
card2: Close enough to reach in a day or two. Far enough that it's not one tap away at the store.
card3: Tell the app how much is in savings right now, so your countdown is exact.

title: What counts as an emergency
card1: Ask three questions: Is it urgent? Is it necessary? Was it unexpected?
card2: A car repair so you can get to work: yes. A great sale or a weekend trip: no. Those get a goal of their own.
card3: If you use the cushion, that's it working. Refilling it comes first, then you pick up where you left off.

title: Make it a payday habit
card1: Plans don't fail on day one. They fail on the third payday, when life gets busy.
card2: Two minutes every payday: give every dollar a job, update your balances, collect your stars.
card3: Turn on payday reminders or add check-ins to your calendar, so payday reminds you.

title: Find your number
card1: Most of us don't have a spending problem as much as a seeing problem. Money leaves in small, quiet amounts.
card2: Today you only have to look. What comes in each paycheck, and what already has a job? No judgment.
card3: Open your budget and read every line. Notice what surprises you. You can't change what you can't see.

title: Sort your spending
card1: A need keeps you housed, fed, healthy and getting to work. A want makes life more fun. Both are fine.
card2: Problems start when wants hide inside needs.
card3: Look at where your money went, store by store. You decide what's a need. Be honest, not harsh.

title: Wants, on purpose
card2: What lasts is choosing your wants ahead of time, so fun money is money you meant to spend.
card3: Pick a fun-money number you can live with. The difference between that and last month is money found.

title: Your $1,000 cushion
card1: A flat tire. A vet bill. A surprise copay. Life happens.
card2: $1,000 set aside means a surprise doesn't land on a credit card. Keep it in a separate savings account you can reach in a day or two.
card3: It's not fun money. It's your shock absorber. If you use it, refilling it comes first. That's the cushion working.

title: Smallest debt first
card1: List every debt except the house, smallest balance to largest.
card2: Pay minimums on everything. Throw every extra dollar at the smallest one.
card3: It isn't always the cheapest math, but it's the math people finish. Each paid-off payment rolls into the next.

title: Name your dream
card1: Saying no is easier when you know what you're saying yes to.
card2: A trip. A car that runs. A Christmas without a credit card.
card3: Name one goal and give it a dollar amount and a date. It shows as a flag at the end of your map.

title: Make it a payday habit
card1: Plans don't fail on day one. They fail on the third payday, when life gets busy.
card2: Two minutes, every payday: give every dollar a job, update your balances, collect your stars.
card3: Turn on payday reminders or add check-ins to your calendar, so payday reminds you.

title: Smallest debt first
card1: List every debt except the house, smallest balance to largest.
card2: Pay minimums on everything. Throw every extra dollar at the smallest one.
card3: It isn't always the cheapest math, but it's the math people finish. Quick wins keep you going.

title: Stop adding new debt
card1: You can't climb out of a hole while you're still digging.
card2: Pause the credit cards while you work the snowball. Pay with your debit card or cash, and let fun money set the limit.
card3: A card can stay open. It just stays home.

title: Roll it forward
card1: When a debt is paid off, its payment doesn't disappear. It rolls to the next smallest debt.
card2: That's the snowball: every payoff makes the next one faster.
card3: On payday, give every dollar a job. The app rolls the money forward for you.

title: Speed it up
card1: Every extra dollar brings payoff day closer.
card2: Sell something you don't use, pick up a shift, or cancel a subscription.
card3: Try one challenge. When it brings in money, your map shows how many paydays you stole back.
